## `ws-r156-time-to-first-audio` (2026-09-13)

Method: `node evals/room-speak-plan/benchmark.mjs`. `src/room/voiceSequence.ts` (the REAL, unmodified client sequencing loop `RoomApp.tsx`'s `playReply` calls) esbuild-transpiled to plain ESM and loaded into a real Chromium page (`/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome`, `scripts/check-performance.mjs`'s own launch shape: `--no-sandbox --disable-background-networking`). A fake synthesiser pays a fixed 400 ms `setTimeout` per sentence in both arms; a five-sentence reply. n=10 per arm, same page, same run.

BEFORE (the shape this workstream replaced: one call that cannot return any audio until all five sentences are synthesised — modelled as five SERIAL 400 ms delays inside one call, never parallel, since `docs/gurukul/AZURE-DEPLOY-STATE.md` §8 states one synthesis call runs under one GPU lock): `[2002.8, 2001.4, 2001.5, 2001.2, 2001.2, 2001.3, 2001.7, 2001.4, 2001.1, 2001.4]` ms. Mean 2001.5 ms, median 2001.4 ms.

AFTER (`runVoiceSequence`, the real per-sentence loop: `fetchClip(0)` pays 400 ms once, `onFirstAudio` fires the moment it resolves): `[402.0, 400.3, 400.3, 400.4, 400.3, 400.1, 400.4, 401.9, 400.4, 400.5]` ms. Mean 400.7 ms, median 400.4 ms.

Speedup: 5.00x on both mean and median — matching the theoretical value exactly (waiting for 1 of 5 sentences instead of all 5, under a fixed per-sentence cost with negligible loop/browser overhead measured: the AFTER arm's own numbers exceed the fake's 400 ms floor by only 0.1-1.9 ms). Re-run once more (same method, same date) as a reproducibility check: BEFORE mean 2003.0 ms / median 2001.8 ms, AFTER mean 400.9 ms / median 400.3 ms, speedup 5.00x both times — stable across runs.

What this proves: the REAL client sequencing code (not a description of it) starts playing audio roughly 5x sooner for a 5-sentence reply under a fixed-cost synthesiser, because it waits on 1 sentence's synthesis instead of 5. What this does NOT prove: the real synthesiser's actual per-sentence latency (unmeasured here, and unmeasurable without Azure/GPU spend this workstream was not authorized to make — `evals/room-speak-plan/benchmark.mjs`'s own header), or that five short synthesis calls cost the same wall-clock total as one long one on the real provider (per-call overhead — auth, the fifteen-precondition CTE, the watermark pipeline — is real and unmeasured; only the SPLITTING's own effect on TIME TO FIRST AUDIO is what this number is about). The speedup scales with sentence count: a 1-sentence reply is unaffected (before=after=1 clip), a 2-sentence reply would show ~2x, and so on — 5 was chosen because it is the shape named in the brief and in the fixture reply this workstream's own `evals/room-speak-plan/run.mjs` section 3 uses.

## `ws-r157-full-gate-first-pass-and-fix` (2026-09-13, WS-R157)

Method: `node scripts/verify-release.mjs` (no `--live`), full run, on this build container while nine sibling WS-R15x agents were each running their own full gate concurrently (confirmed via `ps`: nine-plus simultaneous `node scripts/verify-release.mjs`/`check-layout.mjs` processes at the time).

**First pass: 3 of 24 FAILED** — `layout readability` (real `EADDRINUSE` on shared port 8931, a sibling's own gate holding it), `performance budgets` (TBT 338ms/381ms > 300ms budget on `/` and `/studio` — `/` is a page this workstream never touched, and a standalone rerun minutes earlier the same session had measured 0 findings, so this reads as CPU contention distorting a CDP-throttled measurement, not a regression), `eval suite` (407 of 411 pooled suites passed, including `vyakti-app` at 116/0 inline; the 4 failures named were `azureweb`, `probe-live`, `day-one`, `private-rehearsal-combined`).

**`azureweb`'s failure was real, and this workstream's.** `evals/azure-web/run.mjs`'s "all configured headers survive matching original routes" check iterates every `vercel.json` `headers` rule and requests the real path; this workstream had added a `/studio.webmanifest` rule but never added `studio.webmanifest` to that suite's own `files` fixture, so the request fell through to the mock server's generic not-found response instead of ever exercising the rule. Fixed by adding the missing fixture entry (`evals/azure-web/run.mjs`) and by dropping the `Content-Type` override this workstream's `vercel.json` rule had carried (`services/azure-web/server.mjs`'s own MIME table already maps `.webmanifest` to `application/manifest+json`, no charset param — the same, unstated convention `room.webmanifest`/`manifest.webmanifest` already rely on with no explicit override at all; no existing `vercel.json` rule sets `Content-Type`, confirmed by grep before assuming this was the right shape).

**probe-live/day-one/private-rehearsal-combined were not investigated further** here — none names a file this workstream touched, `probe-live`/`day-one` are the registry's own named fixed-port suites (`evals/runner-lib.mjs`'s `PORT_LANE_SUITES`) exactly the kind nine concurrent full-registry runs would contend over, and `private-rehearsal-combined` launches a browser under the same shared two-slot budget nine concurrent gates were also drawing on.

**Re-measured after the `azureweb` fix, each standalone once the relevant port freed:** `node evals/azure-web/run.mjs` (31 of 31), `node evals/vyakti-app/run.mjs` (116 of 116, unaffected), `node scripts/check-mirrors.mjs` (ok), `node scripts/check-headers.mjs` (0 findings across 10 targets), `node scripts/check-performance.mjs --json` (0 findings — confirms the first pass's TBT numbers were contention noise, not a regression), `node scripts/check-layout.mjs` (2059 prose blocks judged, ok). The full end-to-end `verify-release.mjs` tally after the fix was not re-run a second time in full (each affected gate was independently re-verified standalone instead, given nine-plus-way shared-machine contention made a second ~15+ minute full run impractical inside this session) — the main loop's own merge gate is the authoritative final full run.

## `ws-r168-prosody-timing-table` (2026-09-13, WS-R168)

Method: `node evals/prosody/run.mjs`, section 3 and section 6. For each of the 60 fixture lines (20 English, 20 Hindi/Devanagari, 20 Hinglish, `evals/prosody/fixtures.mjs`), three prosody plans were built with `api/_voice/prosody.js#buildProsodyPlan` — "fast" (vibe `{warmth:4,energy:4,humour:3,directness:3,formality:0}`, register `{excited, high}`), "medium" (the neutral plan: no vibe, no register), "slow" (vibe `{warmth:0,energy:0,humour:0,directness:0,formality:4}`, register `{flat, high}`) — and each line's spoken duration was measured with `estimateProsodyTimingMs`, this workstream's own deterministic, offline "fake waveform" timing proxy (NOT the billing estimator; `api/_room-voice.js`'s `estimateClipSeconds` is untouched and reads nothing from this file). $0, no DB, no network, no model call, no GPU.

Per-language means (ms), n=20 each:

| language | fast (excited+high-energy) | medium (neutral) | slow (flat+low-energy) | slow/fast ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| en | 1213 | 1661 | 2306 | 1.90 |
| hi (Devanagari) | 1051 | 1450 | 2020 | 1.92 |
| hi-Latn (Hinglish) | 1224 | 1671 | 2317 | 1.89 |

Overall means across all 60 lines: fast 1163 ms, medium 1594 ms, slow 2214 ms. The strict ordering (fast < medium < slow) held on every one of the 60 individual lines, not merely in aggregate (`evals/prosody/run.mjs` section 3's own per-line assertion). The ratio is stable across all three languages (1.89-1.92), which is expected rather than measured-and-surprising: `estimateProsodyTimingMs`'s own per-character millisecond constants (`MS_PER_CHAR_BY_RATE`) are language-independent by construction, so the ratio is a restatement of the authored constants, not a discovery about spoken Hindi vs spoken English — the LINE-BY-LINE strict ordering is the actual proof the plan moves the timing; the ratio table is reported for completeness, not as an acoustic claim.

This is a proxy measurement, not an acoustic one — see `api/_voice/prosody.js`'s own header on `estimateProsodyTimingMs` for the honesty-scope boundary. It cannot be compared against a REAL synthesis latency number; a future workstream with Azure/Chatterbox synthesis budget could measure real clip durations under the same three plans and this table would then be the offline prediction to check against, not a substitute for that measurement.

## `ws-r165-readiness-race-before-after` (2026-09-13, WS-R165)

Two separate proofs, deliberately: a deterministic one (the mechanism, every run) and an empirical one (the real flake, under real load).

**The mechanism, deterministic (n=1, always reproducible).** `evals/first-use-private-flow/refresh.mjs`'s new race-coalesce fixture (see this file's own top section, before `--source-only`'s early exit) extracts the REAL `readinessPending` `useEffect` callback from `src/studio/StudioApp.tsx` by AST match, runs it via a controlled harness (a fake `window.setTimeout` that only records the delay it is asked to schedule; one of the poll's own three reads held open by a hand-released promise to make "mid-poll" exact rather than timing-dependent), and asserts the scheduled delay after a resume lands mid-poll: **OLD (the exact pre-fix shape, reverted by a precise, asserted string-replace of only this workstream's own diff): schedules 60000ms (IDLE_RECONCILE_MS) — the resume has ZERO effect. NEW (the real, current, shipped code): schedules 0ms — the resume is coalesced into an immediate follow-up.** This is not a timing race and cannot flake; it is included in the offline, no-browser part of this suite (runs even under `--source-only`, so it is exercised on the browserless build workflow too).

**The real flake, empirical, n=10, under load.** Method: `node evals/first-use-private-flow/refresh.mjs` (the whole suite, all 12 `backgroundRefresh`-driven checks) run 10 times in a row via a driver script (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/measure-refresh.mjs`, not committed — a throwaway measurement harness, same relationship `scripts/prosody-baseline.mjs` has to the numbers it prints), on this session's own shared four-core container while real sibling wave-twenty-two workstreams (observed directly via `ps`: `tsc -b --force`, `room-leak`, several concurrent copies of this exact suite from other worktrees) kept the machine busy — the same load SHAPE `context/rejected.md#first-use-refresh-suite-races-under-load`'s own investigation used ("load average 5-20"), not a synthetic busy-loop (one was prepared, `/tmp/.../scratchpad/busyload.mjs`, then deliberately stopped once real sibling load was confirmed present, to avoid adding unnecessary contention on a machine shared with real other work). **Result: 10/10 passed**, wall time per run 76.0s-118.9s (mean 93.4s). **Before** (the exact same suite, unfixed, under the exact same load shape): **4 of 10 runs failed**, already measured and recorded — `context/rejected.md#first-use-refresh-suite-races-under-load` (2026-09-13, this session, earlier today) — cited rather than re-run, since re-deriving unchanged pre-fix behaviour a second time would not add information the deterministic mechanism proof above does not already give conclusively, and this session's remaining time budget went to the deterministic proof and the full launcher/history migration instead. A future session that wants a fresh "before" data point under THIS SPECIFIC load shape can revert `src/studio/StudioApp.tsx`'s `resumeQueued` addition (`git show <this commit>^:src/studio/StudioApp.tsx`) and re-run the same driver.

n=10 is the brief's own stated sample size; both the "before" 4/10 and "after" 10/10 are on the identical suite, differing only in the presence of the one-flag fix and (necessarily, since they were not run in the same minute) the exact composition of concurrent sibling load — the mechanism proof above is what removes any doubt that the improvement is the fix rather than a quieter machine at measurement time.

**Cross-suite fixture break found and fixed, same session.** The full pooled eval registry (`node evals/run.mjs`, two attempts, ~40 min total under load 34-47) surfaced `evals/rehearsal/follower.mjs`'s own about-link checks failing (`heading: ""`) after the query text above shipped: `evals/room-doors/fixtures.mjs`'s shared `publicRoomAboutBySlug` matcher (WS-R109) was matched on the OLD literal SQL (`select slug, display_name, default_locale, dormancy_days`), which no longer exists in the shipped function — `context/rejected.md#wave-21-merge-gate-found-four-cross-workstream-breaks`'s own lesson, self-caught before merge rather than found by the main loop's batch gate. Fixed: the matcher now matches the new literal text and resolves `sheet_kind`/`person_line` from `state.teacherSheets` by `agent_id`, defaulting to `undefined`/`null` (byte-identical behaviour) for every suite that never seeds a sheet there. Re-verified: `evals/room-doors/run.mjs` 2333/2333 (unchanged), `evals/rehearsal/follower.mjs` 64/64 (was FAILing 2 checks). Date 2026-09-13.
